meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: British Columbia (BC), Canada — provincial corporate registry authority; entity type: BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal_State): Common Law in British Columbia; codified corporate statute (Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57); federal AML/CFT statutes and sanctions regimes apply uniformly; Quebec civil law is not applicable to this BC-domiciled entity
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA — Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally in force 2017), Chapter 8 (Investment)
CPTPP — Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (2018), Chapter 9 (Investment)
Canada-UK Trade Continuity Agreement (2021), including investment-protection provisions
Canada-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, in force 2014) — applicable if PRC-domiciled UBOs are present

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended, and its regulations (FINTRAC regime); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (ss 462.3-462.5) and Part XII.2 (ss 355-362) — money-laundering and proceeds-of-crime offences; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), Parts XVIII (FATCA) and XIX (CRS/GATCA) reporting; Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; Investment Canada Act, RSC 1985, c 28 (1st Supp), s 12 — new-Canadian-business notification by non-Canadians. Provincial (BC): Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (BCBCA), Part 2.1 (ss 51.91-51.96) — Transparency Register of significant individuals; Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 217/2004 (forms and statutory fee schedule).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — BC Transparency Register maintained with the Registrar of Companies; statutory access on demand by FINTRAC, CRA, police and specified public officials; nominee and trust arrangements remain lawful but are fully registrable; public open-volume portal disclosure is not currently active for the BC provincial register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each UBO's full passport biodata page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent passport-authenticating authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the issuing state's competent authority (Canada party to the 1961 Apostille Convention, in force for Canada since 11 January 2024) OR Consular Legalization at the competent Canadian High Commission/Embassy for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or regulated depositary bank; notarized copy by local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / KYC relationship letter for each UBO or authorized signatory
Power of Attorney appointing the BC registered agent and incorporation counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of signing, witnessed and authenticated

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or register-of-members extract of any corporate UBO holding 25% or more of the ULC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or corporate secretary of the parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: BC Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing (post-incorporation, for Merchant-of-Record and bank KYC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BC Corporate Registry — Registrar of Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through Global Affairs Canada Authentication Services (Ottawa) for use outside Canada

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), ss. 10-12 (incorporation and articles), s. 21 (required 'Unlimited Liability Company'/'ULC' name element), s. 24 (name reservation), s. 51 (share issuance), ss. 128-142 (first directors and officers), ss. 191-192 (registered office), ss. 207-212 (corporate records); Business Corporations Act Regulation, BC Reg 366/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Corporate Registry / BC Registries and Online Services, Province of British Columbia (Ministry of Finance), administered through the Corporate Online e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles filed electronically under the BCBCA and BC Reg 366/2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: the BCBCA imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a BC ULC and no escrow account is required; shares may be subscribed for nominal consideration (typically CAD$1).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles be confirmed and the Company adopts its registered office at the address stated in the Notice of Articles, British Columbia, and that the corporate register and records office be established at this address. RESOLVED, that the Board accepts the share subscriptions set out in the share subscription ledger and directs that all issued shares be recorded, with no unpaid capital calls for a micro-SaaS venture. RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, to serve until removed, and that those officers are authorized to execute contracts, banking agreements, and regulatory filings for the subscription-software business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services - Corporate Online (BC Registry Service, Province of British Columbia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a NUANS corporate name pre-screen with a proposed name ending in 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC', submit a Name Reservation Request, and obtain the reservation number valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Request and applicant contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised name reservation or provide a consent/clearance letter from the holder of the conflicting name; refile within the reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of incorporation documents and first director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry - Corporate Online portal (pre-filing validation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the BC Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles, insert the ULC liability clause in the articles, designate the first directors (at least one ordinarily resident in British Columbia), select the authorized share structure, and execute each director's consent to act.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles (registered office address and first directors)
Articles containing the ULC unlimited-liability provision
Consent of each first director to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any validation deficiency and refile; if the registry queries a document, submit an explanatory letter or file an Amending Notice of Articles before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-filing, fee payment, and issuance of certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry - Corporate Online e-filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation package electronically, pay the CAD$350 filing fee (plus optional priority service), and download the automatically generated Certificate of Incorporation and endorsed Notice of Articles.
required_dossiers: Validated Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, remedy the validation flags and re-submit; rejected filings receive a fee credit/refund, and the registry provides a rejection notice identifying the exact statutory defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); WorkSafeBC; Municipal Business Licence Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting, approve the share subscription and officer appointments, open the corporate records register, file the initial notice of directors if required, register for corporate income tax and GST/HST with the CRA, register the employer with WorkSafeBC, and apply for any municipal business licence if a physical office is occupied.
required_dossiers: First board resolutions and share subscription ledger
Completed corporate records and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings are cured by filing the annual report and late-fee payment; a struck-off company may apply for restoration under BCBCA ss. 354-357 and refile any missing government forms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 (software publishing); any ancillary physical office is regulated solely by the local municipal business licence office and WorkSafeBC occupational safety authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (office occupancy only); no federal or provincial industrial/manufacturing operating permit is required for the micro-SaaS business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt - pure subscription-software operations generate no regulated effluent, air emissions, or hazardous waste; no Environmental Assessment or Environmental Management Act permit is implicated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered: no industrial wastewater or VOC discharge limits apply. Residual obligations: office e-waste must be recycled through an authorized processor under the BC Recycling Regulation (BC Reg 449/2004), and leased premises must comply with the municipal stormwater/sanitary sewer by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a virtual micro-SaaS office: no fire certification or civil-defense clearance is required. For a physical office: obtain from the municipality a business-occupancy and fire-safety inspection certificate (BC Fire Code compliance) before occupation; complete structural/load inspection of the leased premises; register the employer with WorkSafeBC to secure the occupational health and safety clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; primary portal: My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE at canada.ca; supplementary provincial registrar for British Columbia: BC Ministry of Finance, BC Tax Services (PST account).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a British Columbia unlimited liability corporation, obtain the BC incorporation certificate from the BC Corporate Registry and then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and the GST/HST program account, normally through the new-registration process in My Business Account or Form RC1. A foreign or non-resident supplier that is not incorporated in Canada may register directly for a CRA BN and GST/HST account under the non-resident registration framework using Form RC1 and must appoint an authorized representative with a Canadian address where required. Because the business uses Paddle or Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record, verify whether the payment platform collects Canadian GST/HST and BC PST on the transactional level; the underlying BC ULC remains separately responsible for its own income tax filing, GST/HST registration obligations, and any PST vendor account for supplies not captured by the merchant of record.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no domestic check-the-box regime; a BC ULC is a taxable Canadian company for Income Tax Act purposes and therefore is otherwise subject to entity-level Canadian income tax. The Pass_Through_Eligible classification relevant here arises under foreign check-the-box rules, principally U.S. Treasury Regulation §301.7701-3: if the ULC is not a per se corporation for U.S. tax purposes, the shareholders may file IRS Form 8832 to classify the ULC as a partnership, a disregarded entity, or a corporation. Any such election must be assessed against the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention, hybrid mismatch rules, and the potential application of subsection 245(1) or other GAAR provisions. For GST/HST purposes, the ULC is a separate 'person' and may hold its own BN and GST/HST accounts independent of the shareholders.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) on taxable software and cloud-based software/SaaS; British Columbia has no HST, so the federal headline rate is 5% and BC PST adds up to 7% for taxable in-province software supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, the small-supplier threshold is C$30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies measured over the current calendar quarter and the trailing four calendar quarters; once exceeded, registration is mandatory. Non-resident suppliers of digital goods and services to Canadian recipients must register for GST/HST when their specified taxable supplies to persons in Canada meet the same general economic threshold (C$30,000), unless an exclusion applies. For BC PST, there is no small-supplier monetary exemption for taxable software/SaaS; every supplier making taxable sales into British Columbia, including non-resident suppliers, must obtain a BC PST vendor account.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a continuous transaction control or real-time fiscal clearance system for GST/HST; there is no government-mandated API clearance, digital stamping, or invoice pre-authorization. CRA accepts electronic GST/HST invoices provided they are legible and contain the prescribed particulars, including the supplier's Business Number, the recipient's name, the date of supply, a description of the supply, the GST/HST rate, and the tax amount. Registered suppliers with qualifying turnover are generally required to file GST/HST returns electronically. BC PST invoices must separately state the PST amount for taxable software and may not show it as included unless the tax is expressly absorbed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of services, including SaaS/cloud services, is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act when made to a non-resident person, provided the service is not performed for the non-resident while that individual is present in Canada and does not relate to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or another excluded Canadian-situated supply. For digital exports, the supplier must have contemporaneous evidence that the recipient's ordinary residence, business establishment, or other place of residence is outside Canada and that the supply is not made to a person registered for GST/HST in a way that changes the place of supply. Export zero-rating for physical goods applies when the goods are exported and the supplier retains documented proof of export; for a Micro-SaaS business, the supply is normally a pure digital service or intangible personal property and no customs declaration is triggered unless bundled with physical media.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Coding Form B13A / Canada Customs Export Declaration for any physical media or hardware exported from Canada
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / courier or postal export record evidencing removal from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice and foreign-currency conversion records demonstrating receipt of offshore payment proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a GST/HST return within four years, and longer in the case of misrepresentation or fraud, to deny zero-rating and claw back input tax credits where the export/non-residence documentation is absent, inconsistent, or unreliable. The penalty regime in section 285 of the Excise Tax Act imposes a minimum penalty of C$250 and up to 50% of the net tax understated or the refund or credit claimed if the false statement or omission was made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence. Retrospective interest is chargeable on any GST/HST or PST shortfall. Fraudulent export zero-rating schemes may lead to criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, loss of registration privileges, and joint or director liability where applicable. BC PST penalties separately apply for failure to register, collect, remit, or maintain proper records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls, mandatory export-receipt surrender, or capital-account conversion quotas. Foreign-exchange reporting, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and prudential obligations may also involve the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, the Canada Border Services Agency, and the Canada Revenue Agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. A British Columbia ULC may receive foreign investment, pay foreign suppliers, remit dividends or other permitted distributions, repay shareholder loans, and convert CAD into foreign currencies without a general central-bank approval. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law solvency and authorization requirements, applicable withholding tax, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds checks, sanctions screening, lender covenants, and bank documentation. A ULC does not obtain automatic tax pass-through treatment under Canadian law; its Canadian tax classification and any foreign tax treatment must be separately confirmed. Canadian residents and entities may have foreign-reporting obligations, including specified foreign property reporting where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio generally applies in Canada. Software subscriptions and cloud-software services normally generate service receipts rather than goods-export proceeds subject to a surrender regime. Receipts may remain in CAD or foreign currency accounts and may be converted at the holder's discretion, subject to contractual, tax, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, payment-provider, and bank reporting requirements. Banks may request invoices, contracts, subscription reports, merchant statements, and proof of the commercial purpose of incoming funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection and treasury operations, but not a substitute for a Canadian operating bank account. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy generally operate as merchant-of-record or payment-platform providers, subject to their own underwriting, restricted-business rules, tax collection processes, reserve policies, settlement currencies, chargeback controls, and payout eligibility. An offshore electronic-money institution may provide collection, virtual accounts, or foreign-currency settlement only where its licence, Canadian solicitation model, correspondent-bank arrangements, sanctions controls, and contractual terms permit the activity. The ULC must maintain accurate beneficial-owner, business-purpose, website, terms-of-service, privacy, refund, customer-location, tax, and source-of-funds information. Platform balances are not necessarily Canadian deposit accounts or CDIC-insured deposits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian law does not universally require all directors to appear physically for corporate-account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted by the selected bank after verification of the corporation, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, control structure, Canadian address, business activity, and source of funds. A bank may require a branch appointment, notarized or certified documents, video identification, Canadian-resident contact information, or an in-person interview, particularly for a newly formed ULC, non-resident ownership, foreign tax residence, complex ownership, virtual-office arrangements, or inconsistent business information. The bank's current policy controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or beneficial owner; ownership information differs across corporate records, tax records, platform accounts, and bank forms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and corporate profile; current British Columbia corporate registry extract; articles and shareholder register; organizational chart; passports and residential-address evidence for all beneficial owners and controllers; signed beneficial-ownership declaration; board resolution; tax-residency forms; written explanation of the ULC ownership and control structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a ULC with unlimited liability, foreign tax classification, or expected pass-through treatment creates uncertainty about tax residence, reporting, or economic ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal-entity classification memorandum; corporate tax-residence analysis; applicable Canadian and foreign tax forms; intercompany and shareholder agreements; solvency and distribution policy; accountant or tax-adviser confirmation; flow-of-funds diagram; explanation of why the ULC is commercially required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity with no Canadian operating history, limited capitalization, no employees, virtual office, or founders located outside Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; product demonstration; domain and website evidence; customer terms; subscription pricing; projected cash-flow statement; founder biographies; lease or registered-office evidence; vendor contracts; development agreements; initial capitalization evidence; board-approved treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming funds from shareholders, related entities, payment platforms, or multiple jurisdictions without a clear transaction purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription, capital-contribution, or loan agreements; board approvals; bank statements showing origin of funds; remittance advice; invoices; platform settlement reports; intercompany pricing support; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narrative; reconciliation tying each receipt to the general ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High payment velocity, consumer refunds, chargebacks, payment aggregation, or merchant-of-record activity inconsistent with the stated lightweight SaaS model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-flow map; merchant-of-record contracts; processor statements; customer geography analysis; refund and chargeback policy; transaction-monitoring thresholds; fraud-prevention procedures; sanctions and prohibited-customer screening policy; monthly reconciliation and reserve methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, cybercrime, fraud, or high-risk-country screening alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity-resolution package; beneficial-owner and controller declarations; adverse-media response; source-of-wealth records; sanctions-screening results; customer and supplier risk assessments; enhanced-due-diligence memorandum; independent legal or compliance opinion where appropriate. Do not attempt to process a transaction while a legally reportable or unresolved sanctions concern remains.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear distinction between Canadian operating revenue, foreign merchant proceeds, shareholder funding, dividends, royalties, and intercompany payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chart of accounts; transaction taxonomy; intercompany agreements; licensing and intellectual-property agreements; invoice samples; transfer-pricing policy; GST/HST analysis; dividend and solvency resolutions; monthly bank-to-ledger reconciliation; documented payment-purpose codes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, paid-in capital, or shareholder loans through the ULC's Canadian bank account using a regulated bank wire or correspondent-bank transfer. The remitter name should match the documented investor or lender. Use an accurate payment purpose such as equity contribution, shareholder loan, or intercompany funding; do not label capital as revenue. Provide the bank with the executed funding instrument, board approval, beneficial-owner information, source-of-funds evidence, remitter details, expected amount and currency, and capitalization or loan-accounting treatment. Reconcile the bank receipt to the corporate ledger and retain SWIFT or equivalent payment records. Do not use personal accounts or unrelated third-party accounts. Confirm whether the transfer creates Canadian withholding, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, debt-forgiveness, or foreign-reporting consequences.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the Canadian operating account, foreign-currency account, regulated payment provider, or correspondent-bank network appropriate to the beneficiary and currency. For ordinary SaaS suppliers, use a documented electronic bank transfer with invoice number, contract reference, beneficiary legal name, bank details, currency, and commercial purpose. SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent may be used for cross-border customer or supplier wires; it is a payment message and not itself evidence of trade compliance. A commercial letter of credit is generally unnecessary for routine digital-service procurement but may be used for eligible equipment or larger cross-border procurement subject to bank approval. Maintain invoices, delivery or service evidence, sanctions screening, tax residency documentation, withholding-tax analysis, and three-way reconciliation among contract, payment, and ledger. Screen beneficiaries and intermediaries before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated Canadian bank or eligible counterparty, supported by an identifiable commercial exposure and documented treasury limits
Non-deliverable forwards where the currency, counterparty, settlement mechanics, and applicable Canadian derivatives rules permit them; NDFs should not be used to evade exchange controls or sanctions

Currency swaps or cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty eligibility, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation, and reporting requirements
Foreign-currency options or collars for documented SaaS receipts, supplier payments, or debt exposures, subject to suitability, premium, accounting, and derivatives-risk controls
Natural hedging by matching foreign-currency receipts and expenditures, supported by a board-approved exposure policy and periodic effectiveness review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Annual Return) for a British Columbia Unlimited Liability Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Corporate Registry – Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months immediately following the anniversary date of incorporation (or amalgamation/continuation) each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of CAD $40 (~USD $30) is added if the annual report is submitted after the 2-month deadline; the company is marked 'not in good standing'; a company failing to file annual reports for two consecutive years may be administratively dissolved by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a private ULC that is not a reporting issuer and does not make a public offering. An independent audit may be required if shareholders holding at least 10% of the issued voting shares demand one under section 200 of the BC Business Corporations Act, or if a shareholder request is made pursuant to the company's articles.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Canadian accounting generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). The entity may choose International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); ASPE is the typical framework for a micro SaaS private enterprise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing is required in British Columbia. The BC Business Corporations Act mandates maintenance of a Company Transparency Register containing prescribed information about individuals with significant control; the register must be updated within 10 days of a change, and the company must provide the register to the Registrar upon request. The BC Annual Report does not include UBO confirmation, but serves to confirm the registered office and directors.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 – USD 5,000 per year (if no audit is triggered, USD 0; if a shareholder-requested independent audit occurs, typical range for a micro SaaS is USD 2,500 – USD 5,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general rate for a non-CCPC ULC (15% federal general + 12% British Columbia general); 11% combined on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income if the ULC is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) (9% federal + 2% BC).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday in Canada. Applicable preferential measures: (i) Small Business Deduction – 9% federal and 2% BC rates on active business income up to CAD 500,000, subject to Canadian-control, associated-corporation business-limit aggregation, and taxable-capital phase-out (CAD 10M–15M); (ii) SR&ED investment tax credits – 15% non-refundable for a non-CCPC, 40% refundable for a CCPC, on qualified Canadian R&D salaries, materials, and contracts; (iii) Accelerated Investment Incentive and Class 50 CCA at 55% declining balance for computer hardware and systems software, with 100% immediate expensing of up to CAD 1,500 of original software inventory cost per year for eligible small CCPCs; (iv) no federal or BC patent-box currently available to a consumer micro-SaaS. ULC status does not confer Canadian tax transparency: the ULC remains a resident corporation fully liable to Part I and BC corporate income tax even when check-the-box disaggregated for U.S. federal tax purposes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_note_en: Federal / BC non-capital losses arising after 2018 may be carried back 3 years and forward 20 years; capital losses carry back 3 and forward indefinitely but are only deductible against capital gains. For a micro-SaaS ULC, treatment of startup losses as non-capital allows carryforward against future subscription income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) incorporating BC corporate tax via T2 Schedule 403 – British Columbia Corporate Income Tax Calculation; filed electronically through CRA-approved software (T2 e-file) or CRA My Business Account (limited), with the return required to be e-filed where gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000 or the return is prepared by a tax preparer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal-period returns are due no later than 6 months after the ULC's taxation year-end; balance due for a non-CCPC ULC is due 2 months after year-end (3 months for a qualifying CCPC associated group business limit; instalment schedule applies where prior-year combined federal/BC tax exceeds CAD 3,000).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name, 15-digit CRA Business Number (BN), jurisdiction of incorporation (British Columbia), taxation year-end, status as resident Canadian corporation, and 'ULC' classification;
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled ULC answers resident-corporation identification because it is incorporated in Canada; enter the U.S. parent beneficial owner only in the 'Controlling corporation' field and cross-reference Form T106.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Boxes 100-120 – Gross Revenue and Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Software subscription revenue (SaaS), in-app purchase and merchant-of-record commission adjustments, hosting cost recharges, FX gains; include accrued income under Canadian GAAP and reconcile to taxable income on Schedule 1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attribution rule: only income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment (i.e., the ULC's Canadian business operations) is taxable in Canada; profits from remote hosting or third-party merchant-of-record (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy) distribution outside Canada must still be reported globally in the T2 if earned through the ULC as the contracting entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 – Net Income (Loss) Before Taxes / Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent reconciliation of accounting pre-tax income to Part I taxable income: add-back of non-deductible insurance premiums? non-deductible 50% meals/entertainment, nondeductible fines, excess capital cost allowance, and intra-group management fees paid to the non-resident parent absent a Part XIII election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany expense allocations from the foreign parent (development, brand, shared services) must meet the arm's-length standard under s. 247 and be reduced by Part XIII WHT or treaty clearance; do not deduct unpaid accrued management fees to the U.S. parent in a non-arm's length Cash-basis? deductions are generally allowed only on an 'amount payable' basis with prescribed interest and timing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 3 – Corporate Investment Income and Active Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Segregation of active business income (subscription revenue) from property income (interest, dividends) to determine small business deduction and refundable dividend tax on hand (RDTOH) computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: With a foreign controlling parent, the ULC is almost certainly a non-CCPC; do not enter a CCPC business limit claim; confirm Canadian-control on Schedule 4 and compute Part I at general rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 403 – BC Provincial Corporate Income Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes BC provincial Part A tax on allocated taxable income for a BC permanent establishment; applies general 12% (or 2% small business rate) less BC investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relevant plug-in fields: 'BC permanent establishment (PE) ratio' – for a ULC with its registered office and management in BC operating through cloud infrastructure, the PE allocation factor is typically 100% unless there is a fixed-base PE in another province or treaty country; treaty PE in the U.S. is irrelevant because the ULC is the Canadian taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes CCA on computer hardware (Class 50, 55% declining balance), systems software (Class 50), purchased application software and website development intangibles (Class 12, 100% CCA where eligible) and leasehold improvements (Class 13).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct development costs twice: internally developed SaaS platform costs capitalized as eligible capital expenditure/CCA must be proven by contemporaneous time-tracking; related-party license recharges must survive the transfer-pricing comparability standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 – Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents / T2 cover page
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses each related-party cross-border transaction: management fees, royalties, interest, services, cost contributions and purchase price; requires country-by-country identification of the related non-resident and methodology applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Filing threshold is exceeded when the aggregate FMV of all non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the taxation year — for a micro-SaaS this is usually not met; nonetheless, when parent recharges or royalty arrangements cross the threshold, T106 and contemporaneous documentation must be filed before the T2 due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty under s. 162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete late month, up to 12 months (max 17%); failure to file T106: CAD 100 per month per form up to CAD 2,500 for information returns (plus CAD 100/24-hour enhanced penalty under the 2024 mandatory-disclosure rules in certain cases); late or deficient T1135: CAD 2,500 minimum and CAD 12,000 maximum per form; target of 0.1% per month? no — precise: CRA may add 0.7%-per-month interest on late balance due at prescribed rate plus 4 points compounded daily; late-filing of a T2 where no tax payable: no penalty unless a penalty provision attaches to a required information return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T1135 – Foreign Income Verification Statement (where the ULC holds specified foreign property exceeding CAD 100,000 cost amount) via CRA My Business Account / e-file
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same T2 due date (6 months after year-end; no separate extended date)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports foreign bank deposits, shares of foreign affiliates, foreign intangibles, intercompany receivables from the US parent, and foreign property used in business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard classification of a shareholder loan receivable from a non-resident parent is a specified foreign property; if the ULC's USD receivables or US treasury balances exceed CAD 100,000, complete T1135 and maintain cost-amount records; intercompany receivable that is a 'trade debt' arising in the ordinary course remains reportable under the same thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: s. 162(7): minimum CAD 2,500 and maximum CAD 12,000 per late/incorrect return; willful omission: CAD 500 per month for up to 24 months (CAD 12,000) plus 50% of the tax benefit? no precise: I'd write: $500 per month up to 24 months where knowingly/inadvertently? Keep: 'failure with false omissions can trigger 24-month $500–monthly penalty and an additional gross-negligence 50% penalty under s. 163.2.'

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Schedule 5? Instead: BC corporate tax is not separately filed; the T2 also constitutes the BC return under the Canada-BC Tax Collection Agreement (no duplicate BC filing).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: BC assessment is issued by CRA on the basis of T2 Schedule 403; BC statute-barred period is the same as the federal 4-year reassessment window (3-year normal), i.e., the CRA can reassess within 4 years for non-negligence cases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC general rate 12%, small-business rate 2% for CCPCs, BC 'loss restriction rules follow ITA 111; BC no standalone branch tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provincial allocation to BC is determined by the ULC's BC permanent establishment assumed 100%; no additional BC return to deliver to BC Ministry of Finance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Errors in the provincial calculation are assessed as federal adjustments by the CRA; late-payment interest on BC tax at the prescribed rate plus 4 points, compounded daily, and BC does not impose its own separate late-filing penalty beyond the federal s. 162(1) amount applied to the combined return (administrative coordination).
